question: A matrix $$A=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$ is transformed by $R_1\rightarrow \frac{1}{2}R_1$ and then $R_2\rightarrow R_2-R_1$. Find the final matrix and identify the type of elementary operation used at each stage.
explanation:
Multiplication of a row by a non-zero number
Applying $R_1\rightarrow \frac{1}{2}R_1$, $$\begin{bmatrix}2 & 4 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\rightarrow\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}$$
This is multiplication of a row by the non-zero scalar $\frac{1}{2}$.
Addition of a multiple of one row to another
Applying $R_2\rightarrow R_2-R_1$, $$\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 3\end{bmatrix}\rightarrow\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
The second operation adds $-1$ times the first row to the second row.
Final matrix
$$\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$

options.A: $\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{bmatrix}$; first operation scales $R_1$ by $\frac12$, second adds $-R_1$ to $R_2$.
options.C: $\begin{bmatrix}1&2\\0&3\end{bmatrix}$; first operation interchanges rows, second scales $R_2$.
options.D: $\begin{bmatrix}2&4\\-1&1\end{bmatrix}$; first operation adds rows, second interchanges rows.
